_doc: T3.5 (D-035, d018). The eight-need ladder is frozen (D-018 3); BOUND grows by milestone. M2 bound Sustenance alone; M3/T3.5 binds Sustenance, Shelter and Comfort against real goods baskets. An UNBOUND need contributes EXACTLY nothing whatever its weight says (T2.6 zero-effect gate). varietyWeight is the D-035-A concentration coefficient INSIDE the satisfaction equation - 0 means the need has no diversity dimension (Shelter: two dwellings' worth of timber is not a more varied roof).

aggregation._doc: D-035-B. CES over BOUND needs with substitution elasticity sigma < 1, replacing d018:52's weighted sum. rho = (sigma-1)/sigma < 0 makes needs genuine COMPLEMENTS: surplus comfort cannot buy off absent shelter. sigma 0.5 (rho = -1, the weighted harmonic mean) is the round value squarely inside the non-compensatory regime and far from the sigma=1 Cobb-Douglas degeneration. satisfactionFloor states how bad ONE need at zero is allowed to make the aggregate: at exactly zero the CES limit is 0 regardless of everything else - true in the limit, but it would make a world with nothing indistinguishable from a world with almost nothing and every settlement equally, maximally aggrieved. 0.05 says total deprivation of a single need is very bad, not infinitely bad. It is a MECHANISM PARAMETER, not a guard - raising it weakens non-compensation continuously - and the D-035-B acceptance ceiling is DERIVED from it, never chosen alongside it.
aggregation._tierADoc: d018:46, retained unchanged by D-035-B and applied to the WEIGHTS before aggregation. Below tierAFloor a gate need (Sustenance/Shelter/Safety) scales superlinearly and collapses upper-need weights toward zero: a starving intelligentsia riots over bread, not press freedom. tierAFloor 0.5 = 'half-fed is where the ladder inverts'; tierAGain 3.0 = a wholly unmet gate need weighs 4x its normal weight; tierACollapse 1.0 = upper weights fall linearly in gate severity toward zero.

baskets._doc: D-035-C path 1 (SHARED SATISFIER) and path 2 (SHARED BUDGET) made data. One entry per (class, need, good); perPersonYear is a per-sim-year rate integrated with dtYears (law 3), never a per-turn amount. FOOD entries are denominated in PERSON-YEAR-EQUIVALENTS of nutrition, the D-015 convention grain already carries: a class's food entries sum to 1.0 by construction, so the basket changes WHAT is eaten and never how much nutrition a person needs. Peasants eat a staple diet; artisans, with income and a market, eat measurably more livestock and fish - the T3.5 class-differentiation requirement IS this table, not a coefficient bolted on afterwards. SUBSTITUTION: unmet non-staple food demand falls back on the staple (grain), because a household short of fish eats more bread rather than going hungry while grain sits in the store. Monotony is then paid for in the D-035-A variety term rather than in calories, which is exactly the director's rationale - a settlement that can feed itself entirely on grain still has a reason to import fish. SHELTER is an upkeep flow of dwelling materials, an honest M3 stand-in for the housing STOCK T3.8 builds: a settlement short of timber cannot keep its roofs up, which is what 'a housing shortage lowers Shelter satisfaction' can mean before there is a housing stock to be short of. TUNE, all of it.
